summary: Discovery on integration patterns for HelioWorks' conversational platform. Discussed SDKs, LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limiting and quotas, and observability hooks. Team evaluated tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) options for latency/cost/compliance. Agreed to pilot a Hosted+gateway proxy flow for quick validation and run a short dedicated capacity benchmark if SLA looks necessary.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-19 16:00 PT | Duration: ~56m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Clara Huang (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (HelioWorks Head of Platform), Devon Klein (Staff ML Eng), Priya Nair (Security)

[00:00] Samir: all right hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, I know you have a packed week so we'll keep it focused. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Clara, our systems SE who'll walk through integrational patterns.
[00:08] Marta: hey thanks Samir, yeah we're excited to uh just understand how we plug Redwood into our stack. we're running a conversational agent that backs support and a few internal bots, latency is a big thing for us.
[00:15] Devon: hi all, quick intro — i'm devon, i own the runtime layer. our infra is k8s EKS, we have an api gateway in front of everything and we're looking at either plugging Redwood via SDK calls from the gateway or running a proxy sidecar.
[00:28] Clara: great, that's exactly what we'll cover. quick agenda: SDK options, LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors, proxy/gateway patterns, quotas/rate limiting, observability/tracing, then next steps. does that sound good?
[00:36] Marta: yep good.
[00:38] [00:45] Samir: quick question on compliance — priya, are there any hard constraints? VPC only, KMS for keys, that sort of thing?
[00:52] Priya: hi, yes, we're SOC2 in progress, we need customer-managed keys for secrets if we go private, and for any hosted flow we require audit logs and SSO via SAML, plus data residency for EU traffic.
[01:05] Samir: totally understood. Redwood supports SAML/SSO, audit logs in the console, and the private deployment supports KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include that in the security doc.
[01:13] Devon: can you explain the difference in network flow between Hosted and Private, specifically if we keep our gateway and just call Redwood?
[01:22] Clara: yeah. Hosted is a simple outbound API call from your gateway to our public endpoint — easiest to get started, lowest time-to-value. Dedicated is similar but your traffic is pinned to reserved capacity backends for predictable latency. Private (VPC/on-prem) places the serving runtime in your network — traffic never leaves your VPC. The tradeoffs are typical: Hosted quickest, Dedicated predictable at scale, Private best for strict compliance and data residency.
[01:45] Marta: okay, and how do we handle request routing? we have some sensitive routes that need private handling and others that can be hosted.
[01:53] Clara: you can route by policy — path-based or header-based. Many customers run a small proxy in their VPC that inspects routes and forwards to either Redwood-hosted endpoints or the Private deployment. Alternatively, use our SDK with a routing hook that picks model/endpoint based on metadata.
[02:08] [02:15] Devon: are there pre-built connectors for LangChain or LlamaIndex? our retrieval pipeline is LlamaIndex-based, we don't want to rework that.
[02:22] Clara: yes we have sample connectors — LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters — and we've seen teams plug them in with minimal changes. i'll share a repo after the call. note: sometimes names are slightly off in ASR, sorry — LlamaIndex spelled a lot of ways in transcripts.
[02:35] Samir: (laughs) noted.
[02:38] [02:45] Marta: what's the recommended pattern if we want to keep embeddings in our infra but call Redwood for generation?
[02:52] Clara: common approach: keep embeddings/DB local, send context slices to Redwood through the SDK or proxy, and use prefix KV caching to reduce token cost for static context. Also you can send embedding vectors as part of the retrieval step without storing vectors in Redwood.
[03:08] Devon: okay, latency — we need 150–200ms 95th pct for short assistant prompts. is that realistic on Hosted?
[03:17] Clara: Hosted can be variable depending on region and model; small models on hosted often hit that, but production customers needing strict SLOs typically use Dedicated or Private in-region deployment. With Dedicated you get reserved GPUs and better tail latency. There are also batching tradeoffs — continuous batching improves throughput but can raise single-request tail latency unless you configure low-latency lanes.
[03:40] Priya: on rate limits and quotas, we have bursty periods. our gateway imposes 10k rps limits upstream — we'll need to align. what kind of quota enforcement do you provide?
[03:51] Clara: Redwood supports per-token and per-route quotas, token-based throttling, and per-customer rate limiting. You can set burst windows and smoothing. Many customers implement token budgeting at gateway level and rely on Redwood to enforce hard caps.
[04:06] [04:15] Devon: if we put a proxy sidecar, can it do local caching and prevent duplicate requests to Redwood?
[04:21] Clara: yes, sidecar can implement prefix cache and strong de-duplication. Also recommended is a local in-memory cache for short TTLs and use Redis for longer live caching. We can provide best-practice examples.
[04:35] Marta: curious about SDK languages — we use Go for our gateway and Python for the retrieval/LLM layer.
[04:43] Samir: Redwood SDKs cover Python, Node, and Go (beta). The Go SDK supports streaming responses and request middleware to inject routing headers. For LangChain/LlamaIndex, the Python adapters are most mature.
[04:57] [05:00] Devon: about observability — what signals do you emit? we want tracing across the request from gateway -> Redwood -> model runtime -> back.
[05:09] Clara: we emit request-level traces, token-level timing (token generation phases), per-request cost metadata, model version, node latency breakdowns, and we surface these via logs, metrics (prometheus endpoint), and distributed tracing headers (W3C traceparent). You can hook our tracing into your existing APM.
[05:28] Marta: do you expose token-level timing in Prometheus or only in logs?
[05:33] Clara: token timing is available in structured logs and the console per request; we also provide aggregate histograms as metrics for latency buckets.
[05:42] [05:45] Priya: for compliance we need immutable audit logs showing prompt/response hashes, who accessed what, and retention policies.
[05:53] Samir: we have audit logs with configurable retention; for hosted we can hash prompts and store hashes in audit trails; Private gives you full control to store raw logs inside your environment. We'll include examples in the security pack.
[06:06] Devon: question on costs — if we cache prefixes aggressively does that materially reduce billed tokens?
[06:13] Clara: yes. caching and KV reuse are two of the largest levers to cut per-token costs. With prefix cache you avoid re-sending static context, you pay for the generated tokens and any dynamic context. Redwood Optimize can suggest cache/quantization settings per workload.
[06:28] [06:35] Marta: we'd like a quick pilot: start with Hosted to validate outputs and then potentially move to Dedicated for predictable latency. is that doable?
[06:44] Samir: absolutely, that's a common path. pilot flow: we provision a sandbox hosted org for you, run a small load-generation test, share observability dashboards, then if you like performance we scope a dedicated capacity benchmark.
[06:57] Devon: for the benchmark, what data and test harness do you need from us?
[07:03] Clara: a few prompt templates, expected seq lengths, concurrency targets, and a sample retrieval pipeline shape. also let us know which model families you want to test. We'll provide a k6 locust-style script and can run it against Hosted or Dedicated.
[07:19] [07:25] Marta: can Redwood be fronted by our existing API gateway with an oauth token or do we need a proxy? we want minimal infra changes.
[07:33] Clara: you can call Redwood from your gateway with OAuth or API key. Many teams prefer to put minimal logic in the gateway and use a small auth proxy to rotate keys and add routing headers. If you want zero infra changes, call Hosted direct via SDK from your application layer.
[07:47] Devon: any pitfalls integrating with LlamaIndex retrieval layers? we've run into TTL mismatches and vector mismatch issues before.
[07:55] Clara: common issues: sequence length assumptions in retrieval, tokenization differences between retrieval and serving model, and batching mismatches. Our connectors include tokenization helpers and examples of chunking to avoid OOMs. We'll share the adapter that includes a small shim to normalize chunking and token limits.
[08:12] [08:20] Priya: one more — encryption in transit and at rest for hosted — we require TLS 1.2+ and envelope encryption.
[08:27] Samir: Redwood supports TLS 1.2/1.3, and for hosted we provide encrypted storage; if you need envelope encryption / customer-managed keys that's supported in Private or via an enterprise plan for hosted where we can integrate KMS.
[08:40] Marta: ok sounds good.
[08:43] [08:50] Samir: quick demo idea — Clara, want to walk them through a simple LangChain flow now or save for follow-up?
[08:56] Clara: i can do a 8–10 min sketch. i'll share my screen — sorry the ASR sometimes misses code snippets.
[09:05] [09:15] Clara: (screen share) here's a Python snippet using our client: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...). Then a LangChain wrapper: RedwoodLLMWrapper(llm=client, model='rwd-small-1'). See how we pass a routing header 'x-tenant-route' to choose hosted vs private in middleware?
[09:33] Devon: looks clean. can we inject our own traceparent?
[09:36] Clara: yes, pass trace headers and we will propagate them through the runtime.
[09:41] [09:50] Marta: what's the recommended approach to enforce quotas per product? we have multiple products sharing the same org.
[09:56] Clara: per-route quotas keyed by product id header is typical. Redwood console allows per-route token budgets and alerting when thresholds are close.
[10:10] Devon: if we use Dedicated, can we split capacity per product?
[10:15] Samir: with Dedicated you can partition pools and have capacity reservations per team or product. billing can be chargebacked via tags.
[10:24] [10:30] Marta: any mandatory agent-side changes for streaming responses? we use SSE in our gateway.
[10:36] Clara: our streaming API is compatible with SSE and websockets; the SDK includes a streaming client that emits chunk events. The Go SDK beta supports streaming and backpressure handling.
[10:49] Priya: remediation question — if there's a data incident, how quickly can Redwood provide logs?
[10:55] Samir: for hosted tier we provide a support runbook and we can export logs; dedicated and private give you more direct access to logs and faster response SLAs. We'll include SLAs in the next doc.
[11:08] [11:15] Devon: what about tokenization mismatch across models if we switch model families in a rollout?
[11:21] Clara: we recommend versioned rollouts and running pre-flight evals against held-out prompts — Redwood Console supports canary rollouts with automatic fallbacks. Tokenization diffs are highlighted in eval reports.
[11:35] Marta: good. ok, i think we have the gist. final ask — can you send a short README with the connector snippets and a proposed pilot plan?
[11:43] Samir: yes — we'll send a 1-page pilot plan plus connectors and security pack.
[11:48] Priya: let's set a SOC2 Q&A next week, prefer Thurs 2027-02-25.
[11:54] Samir: noted. we'll loop in our security lead.
[11:58] [12:00] Devon: thanks everyone.
[12:02] Marta: thanks both.
[12:04] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts. bye.

Notes on transcript: occasional ASR hiccups (e.g., k v cache / K-V cache written differently), speaker overlap noted as [crosstalk], some proper nouns mis-capitalized.

References & links mentioned during call: "LangChain / LlamaIndex adapter repo (to be shared)", "Security pack (SOC2, audit logs, KMS)"
